clue.text: Sculpture, perhaps, of Trump grabbing popular chanteuse's backside

indicators.note: the first piece grabs and holds the others inside it

parts.note: to trump is British slang for breaking wind, so a trump is a fart
IN means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: the backside of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A satirical statue of a former US president groping a singer's behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' looks like the politician, but it is British slang for breaking wind. FART grabbing IN and E (the end of chanteuse) gives F-INE-ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculpture is one example of the visual arts produced for beauty rather than use.

clue.text: Finishing with dual nationality?

parts.note: a wood finish whose two-word name is two nationalities, from France and from Poland

explanation.walkthrough: The finish is a glossy shellac treatment for wooden furniture; its name happens to join two nationality adjectives.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellac-based polish applied by hand gives furniture its glossy surface, a finishing treatment.

clue.text: Young child damaged linen rugs

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of shape, so the fodder is rearranged

explanation.surface: A toddler has ruined some soft furnishings made of linen.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurseling is an infant still being nursed, so a baby or very small child.

clue.text: On the beach, wash more when taking tops off

indicators.note: the top of each word in a down clue is its first letter, and both are removed

explanation.surface: Advice for laundering beachwear, or for sunbathers stripping off.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land beside the sea, which is where a beach lies.

clue.text: Where a pig might go to get warm?

definitions.text: Where a pig might go to get warm?

parts.words: Where a pig might go to get warm?
parts.note: a pig's home is its pen, a sty; read the answer as a three-word route to that pen

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as TO A STY, where a pig might go; as one word it means warm and cosy.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasty is an informal adjective for pleasantly cosy and heated, and a sty is a pigpen.

clue.text: Tip the Queen's physician

parts.note: to tip is to lean over, to list
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: An instruction to give a gratuity to the royal doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Lister was the British surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister was a famous Victorian surgeon, a medical man known for antisepsis.

clue.text: Maybe Ivy excited to avoid constant exercise

indicators.note: the climber steers clear of the constant, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: ivy is an example of a climbing plant, a climber
C is the symbol for a constant (and the speed of light)
UP means excited, worked up

explanation.surface: Someone called Ivy is too worked up to keep up a steady workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ivy' reads as a woman's name but is the plant. CLIMBER avoiding C gives LIMBER, then UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To limber up is to warm up the muscles before sport, a phrasal verb for exercising.

clue.text: Ashen, but remedy this?

indicators.note: to remedy is to put right, so these letters are set straight into a new order

explanation.surface: Looking pale? Here is the cure.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rearranging ASHENBUT gives the cure for looking pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in the sun is the obvious cure for a pallid, colourless complexion.

clue.text: Intersex celebrity's inspiring top

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the phrase takes the letters inside it

explanation.surface: An intersex star's role model or uplifting quality is praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like a noun but works as a verb, to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is to beat or outdo them, which is to excel.

clue.text: Want to ignore the first world

indicators.note: the opening letter of the synonym is left out

parts.note: want means lack or scarcity, a dearth

explanation.surface: A wish to disregard the developed nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as a verb but is the noun meaning shortage.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is our planet, the world we live on.

clue.text: Cooked macaroni in rotating glass bowls

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared and changed, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Pasta prepared in spinning glass serving dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowls' looks like crockery for the pasta, but it describes the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Franklin's glass harmonica is played on nested spinning glass bowls touched by wet fingers.

clue.text: Firearm "a small, trivial matter," claims man yet to see the light

indicators.note: the outer letters claim, take in, the man

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a trifle is something of little importance

parts.words: man yet to see the light
parts.note: Saul was the apostle Paul's name before his conversion on the Damascus road

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a gun as unimportant, quoting a stubbornly unconverted man.
explanation.walkthrough: Saul was blinded by light on the road to Damascus and renamed Paul, so before that moment he had not yet seen the light.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault rifle is an automatic military weapon, a type of gun.

clue.text: Skin rabbit's head in Vauxhall

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Chevette was a small Vauxhall car

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A grisly instruction to flay a rabbit in a car or in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Vauxhall is a British car maker (also a London area); its 1970s-80s small car was the Chevette.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevrette is a soft leather made from goatskin, kid leather.

clue.text: Bas-reliefs regularly seen in Van Gogh's home

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at a steady interval, here every second one

explanation.surface: Carved sculptures often appear in the painter's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincent van Gogh lived and painted in Arles, in Provence, in 1888-89.

clue.text: Set melody on piano

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Put a tune on the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb but is the noun, a matched group.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a matching set of two items.

clue.text: A lot of tea bags are for Spanish maid

indicators.note: to bag is to capture, so the outer letters hold the unit inside

parts.note: much means a lot
cha is a slang word for tea
a is the symbol for the are, a metric unit of area

explanation.surface: Tea bags are plentiful for a Spanish housemaid.
explanation.walkthrough: The are is a metric unit of 100 square metres; bags puts its symbol A between MUCH and CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Muchacha is Spanish for girl, used especially of a young female servant.

clue.text: Charlotte perhaps meeting sick war hero

parts.note: Charlotte Church is a Welsh singer
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A woman called Charlotte visits an unwell soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlotte Church is a Welsh singer famous as a child soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill led Britain through the Second World War, a celebrated wartime leader.

clue.text: Music producer in Spain covered in mud

indicators.note: the mud covers the other letters, which sit inside it

parts.note: clart is a Scots and northern English dialect word for mud
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Someone producing music in Spain gets plastered in mud.
explanation.walkthrough: CLART covers IN plus E, giving CLAR-INE-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument, something that makes music.

clue.text: Be the Chancellor: mostly disagreeable

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live

indicators.note: most of the name is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Rishi Sunak was the UK Chancellor of the Exchequer

explanation.surface: Taking the finance minister's job is mostly unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The UK Chancellor of the Exchequer is the finance minister; Rishi Sunak held the post 2020-22.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverish means irritable and grumpy, as if from a disordered liver.

clue.text: Lied about hosting party, getting funds to fight case

indicators.note: the rearranged letters host the party inside
about suggests the letters are turned around in a new order

parts.note: a gala is a festive party

explanation.surface: Someone lied about holding a party to raise money for a court battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIED into LE ID, which hosts GALA: LE-GALA-ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal aid is public money paying lawyers for people who cannot afford litigation.

clue.text: Confrontation expected by Labour leader

parts.note: due means expected

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A political showdown anticipated by the head of the Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal fight between two people, a confrontation.

clue.text: Exit for one on steamship

parts.note: EG, for example, means for one
RE means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A way out for a single passenger on a steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is a way out, the opposite of an entrance.

clue.text: Valiant prince gets blessed

parts.note: to be blessed is to be fortunate, lucky

explanation.surface: A brave royal receives a blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucky means brave and spirited, courageous.

clue.text: Delightful plastic purse

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters can be reshaped

explanation.surface: Admiring a handbag made of plastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal praise meaning excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: Frank left in distress

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pain is suffering, distress

explanation.surface: A man called Frank was abandoned and upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain speaking is candid and direct, so plain means outspoken.

clue.text: Nits, present and future, start to ruin kitchen implement

parts.note: nits are lice eggs: now they are eggs, later they will be lice

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Head lice, now and to come, begin to spoil a cooking gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: A nit is the egg of a louse, so in the present it is EGGS and in the future LICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg slicer is a wired kitchen gadget that cuts boiled eggs into neat slices.

clue.text: Mum queuing to take drug intravenously

parts.note: ma is a word for mother
people queuing stand in line

explanation.surface: A mother waiting her turn to inject herself.
explanation.definitionFit: To mainline is slang for injecting a narcotic directly into a vein.

clue.text: Halogens found in steep rock face

parts.note: read as chemical symbols, the four pieces are chlorine, iodine, fluorine and fluorine again, all halogen elements

explanation.surface: Chemical elements discovered in a sheer rock wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Halogens are the group of reactive elements including chlorine (Cl), iodine (I) and fluorine (F); split the answer into those symbols and it spells out halogens.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliff is a high, sheer wall of rock, often at the coast.

clue.text: Grab son, of course

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
natch is slang for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: A parent says naturally they will grab the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To snatch is to seize something quickly, a synonym of grab.

clue.text: Shade thrown: be sulky

indicators.note: thrown letters are tossed and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has been insulted and is told to sulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade thrown' looks like the slang for an insult, but Shade is the colour definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky blue is a pale tint of blue, a colour shade.
